evaluations.model_answer:
Given that StrmLLM (n=64) achieves a lower final loss than Vanilla at iteration 140,000, what architectural advantages of streaming attention might explain this superior convergence?
Streaming attention allows the model to process the input sequence sequentially, attending to only the relevant parts of the sequence at each step. This can be more efficient than traditional self-attention, which attends to all parts of the sequence simultaneously.  The sequential processing might lead to faster convergence by reducing the computational burden and potentially allowing the model to focus on the most important information earlier in the training process.  It could also help with longer sequences by mitigating the quadratic complexity of standard self-attention.
